text:
A: Hiya! Last one, isn't it? I'm Nicola.
B: Tariq. Hi. Yeah, last one.
A: How've you found it? I've had a lovely time, everyone's been so chatty.
B: It's been fine. Better than I expected, honestly.
A: Ha, what did you expect?
B: Three minutes of talking about the weather. It's been more interesting than that.
A: Well, I'll try not to mention the weather then. So what do you do, Tariq?
B: Operations for a facilities management company in London. Cleaning, security, maintenance contracts for office buildings. You?
A: I'm a dental hygienist, two days a week in Frome. In Somerset.
B: Right. So you're the one who tells people off about flossing.
A: No! I never tell anyone off. That's the whole trick, you chat them through it, you ask about their grandkids, and they don't even notice you're scraping away. It's sort of like being a hairdresser, only with more blood.
B: That's a terrible selling point.
A: Ha, yeah, don't put that on the leaflet. You drink a lot of coffee, I reckon. You've got the look.
B: Sorry, what look is that exactly?
A: I don't know, organised. Busy. Bit tired round the eyes. Sorry, that's rude!
B: No, it's accurate. Three or four a day. I'm fussy about it, though, there's a new place by Stratford station that's actually decent.
A: Well, I won't lecture you. Do you get away much, with a job like that?
B: One proper trip a year. Japan was the last one. Before that Uzbekistan, Samarkand and Bukhara. And Andalusia, for the Alhambra.
A: Oh, I've always wanted to see the Alhambra! I did Lisbon with my girlfriends. Was it worth it?
B: Completely. Go early, book the Nasrid Palaces slot weeks ahead, and go to Córdoba as well, the Mezquita. People skip Córdoba and they shouldn't. It's about two hours on the train, there's a fast one from Granada now, and honestly the inside of the Mezquita, all those arches going on and on in the half-dark, it's one of the best buildings I've ever stood in.
A: See, now I want to go. You'd be a proper good person to travel with, you'd know where everything was.
B: I would. I'd also want to leave at seven in the morning.
A: Ah, that's me out then. I'm more of a sit at the next table and make friends with the waiter sort of person. I'm going to New Zealand one day, that's my big one.
B: One day meaning when?
A: Erm, once Alfie's done his GCSEs and I've saved up. So, never, probably!
B: Put a date on it. Then work back from the date. Otherwise it stays "one day".
A: That's proper sensible. Annoyingly sensible. Do you do that with everything?
B: Pretty much. My mum says I'd plan breakfast if she let me.
A: Ha! I like your mum already. Has she got—
